title: Whether there was faith in Christ's soul; and whether the saints already translated to heaven have face-to-face knowledge of God
pass_a_gloss: Article XII. Whether there was faith in Christ's soul; and whether the saints already translated to heaven have face-to-face knowledge of God. 1. Concerning faith in Christ's soul: Orthodox theologians commonly deny that faith was in Christ's soul as wayfarer in the same way as in us, because Christ from the first moment of conception had clear and beatific vision of God; but faith and vision do not stand together in the same subject concerning the same object. 2. Some nonetheless distinguish: Christ as wayfarer knew certain things by faith as to the state of outward humiliation; but it is safer to say that his cognition of divine things was always superior to faith, because he was personally united to the Logos. 3. Concerning the saints in heaven: they do not have faith, but vision. Faith is evacuated in the homeland, 1 Corinthians 13. For when we shall see face to face, we no longer walk by faith. They have face-to-face knowledge of God — not indeed infinite comprehension, but intuitive and beatific vision according to the creature's capacity.
pass_b_english: Article XII. Whether there was faith in Christ's soul; and whether the saints already translated to heaven have face-to-face knowledge of God.

1. Orthodox theologians commonly deny that faith was in Christ's soul as in ours. From conception he had clear beatific vision of God; faith and vision do not coexist in the same subject about the same object.
2. Some say Christ as wayfarer knew some things by faith in his outward humiliation. Safer: his knowledge of divine things was always above faith, because he was personally united to the Logos.

3. Saints in heaven have not faith but vision. Faith is evacuated in the homeland (1 Corinthians 13). Seeing face to face, they no longer walk by faith. They have facial knowledge of God — not infinite comprehension, but intuitive beatific vision according to creaturely capacity.
source_text:
ART. XII.
An fides fuerit in anima CHRISTI? & an sit in Sanctis, qui jam in coelum translati, habeant DEI cognitionem facialem, ut loquuntur.

1. De fide in anima CHRISTI: Theologi Orthododoxi communiter negant fidem fuisse in anima CHRISTI viatoris eodem modo quo in nobis, quia CHRISTUS a primo conceptionis momento visionem DEI claram & beatificam habuit; fides autem & visio simul in eodem subjecto quoad idem objectum non consistunt.

2. Aliqui tamen distinguunt: CHRISTUS ut viator quaedam per fidem cognovit quoad statum externaе humiliationis; sed tutius est dicere cognitionem ejus de rebus divinis semper fuisse superiorem fide, quia personaliter unitus erat Λόγῳ.

3. De Sanctis in coelo: illi non habent fidem, sed visionem. Fides evacuatur in patria, 1 Cor.13. Cum enim videbimus facie ad faciem, non amplius per fidem ambulamus. Habent cognitionem facialem DEI — non quidem comprehensionem infinitam, sed visionem intuitivam & beatificam secundum capacitam creaturae.
